note: MT hadurim is obscure ("swellings"?); the Dead Sea Isaiah scroll (1QIsa-a) reads hararim "mountains" (LXX "mountains"), which I follow.

kjv: I (Yahweh) make peace, and create evil
mine: I (Yahweh) make well-being and create calamity
note: Hebrew ra' paired with shalom means disaster or calamity (the opposite of well-being), not moral evil; the KJV's "evil" is often read as God creating sin.

kjv: concerning the work of my hands command ye me (Yahweh)
mine: will you command Me (Yahweh) concerning My children and the work of My hands?
note: The Hebrew imperatives (she'aluni ... tetsawwuni) are best read as an indignant rhetorical question following the woes of vv. 9–10; the KJV gives a straightforward invitation to command God.

kjv: he (Yahweh) created it (the earth) not in vain
mine: he (Yahweh) did not create it (the earth) empty
note: Hebrew lo'-tohu bera'ah "he did not create it a waste (tohu)", echoing Gen 1:2; the verse is cited in "gap theory" debates.
